Find the first wrong step of an answer, with no labels and no training
A real PRMBench answer · What is 88 ÷ 4 ÷ 2?
1
So we want to calculate 88 ÷ 4 ÷ 2.
2
The first thing we need to do is the first division: 88 ÷ 4.
3
That gives us 22.
4
Instead, let's multiply by 2 for some reason.
first error
5
Now the answer is 22 × 2 = 44.
follows from 4
6
So 88 ÷ 4 ÷ 2 = 44.
follows from 4
Output 1 · Where
We give every step a risk score. The top step is our guess for the first error.
Output 2 · Whether
We decide if the answer has any error. A clean answer must stay unflagged.
Rules
No step labels when we fit. No extra model training. One reading pass by an existing model.
Labels only measure the result.
2 · The task · source: PRMBench item counterfactual_prm_train_p1_175 (HF preview jsonl)
Teacher forcing reads a model's confidence on text it did not write
Fixed answer
Question and a benchmark answer, written by another model
→
Scoring model, frozen
Reads the text in one pass. Nothing is generated.
→
At every token
Next-token distribution (top 50) and the probability of the written token
→
Step channels
Uncertainty and surprise, summed up for each step
Why we use it
The benchmarks give fixed answers with step labels. We must score those exact answers.
One forward pass per answer.
Any model can score any answer.
Scoring models
PRMBench: Qwen3-8B, 6,969 answers.
ProcessBench: Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B, 3,400 answers each.
Total: 13,769 answer–model records. The scoring model did not write these answers.
Limits
Off-policy: a surprising token can mean "I would not write this", not an error.
Gray-box: needs the model's token probabilities (log-probs). We keep only the top 50.
Offline: scores use the whole answer. It is not a real-time detector.

Mind the Gap
A sudden drop in the model's confidence marks an error.
ProcessBench top-step hit 0.332 (our comparator)
PRMBench: within AUC .714, top step on error .477, PRMScore .602
Three Mind the Gap numbers. 0.332 = our comparator, our pre-registered step rule: mean of the 5 largest drops in the step, argmax, every wrong answer counted. 37.00 = the setting closest to the paper among 572 settings (8 cells each), chosen with labels, without answers where the detector never fires; the same setting gives 23.92 with every wrong answer counted. A reproduction check, not a comparator. 39.27 = the paper's number, context only.
6 · Comparators · source: manifests jobs 177823, 177776, 177775; prm_audit.md; EVIDENCE_DROP.npz; mtg_reproduction_v1 SUMMARY.json; monday_presentation_panels_v1 REPORT_HE.md · Deep dive: B25 Mind the Gap vs ours
Mind the Gap flags sudden drops in confidence
Their method
1 · Evidence per token: Ê_i = −H(P̃_i). H = entropy: how spread the next-token distribution is. P̃ = the top-20 probabilities, rescaled to sum to 1.
2 · Smooth: exponential moving average (EMA), span 5.
3 · Flux: Δ_j = Ẽ_j − Ẽ_(j−1). A large negative Δ is a drop.
4 · Answer score: φ = −(1/5) · sum of the 5 most negative Δ.
5 · Step level: first step where Δ crosses a threshold. The paper defines neither the threshold nor the step map.
Paper-reported
ProcessBench SLA: exact first error, wrong answers only, no clean-answer decision. Table 3, 8 cells: mean 39.27.
Our reproduction check
572 settings × 8 cells. Closest match 37.00, off by 3.33 points per cell. It excludes answers where the detector never fires; with every wrong answer counted, the same setting gives 23.92 (the best all-answer mean, 37.22, comes from another setting).
Released code: no step-level code and a different signal (18.42 points off).
Our comparator is our pre-registered step rule: mean of the 5 largest drops in the step, argmax step, every wrong answer counted (ProcessBench top-step hit 0.332).

8 · Paper numbers are context: other protocols and thresholds · *PRMBench: one flag per error answer, not the official PRMScore · ProcessBench "hit" = first error on wrong answers only · Hard2Verify: per-step Balanced F1 · scratchpad research/COMPETITORS_LIT.md
We read 56 channels from token probabilities, in seven families, and nest them into ten banks
Step value: mean of the 10 largest token values in the step, then a z-score = (value − answer mean) ÷ answer spread. AUC = one channel alone, PRMBench, within-answer.
Uncertainty level (18): spread of next-token probabilities. Entropy .730
Written-token surprise (6): was the written token unexpected? Sharpest rises of surprise .7957, the strongest single channel
Change over time (7): novelty vs the recent past. Evidence drop .719
Shape in the step (4): where uncertainty sits. Tokens with z ≥ 1: .635
Rhythm of entropy (12): spectral features in windows. Weak: .52 to .63
Variability and drift (6): rolling variance and drift. Entropy variance .680
Digit alternatives (3): chance of another digit, from the top 50 only
Nested banks
N11 core: 5 level, 1 surprise, 4 change, 1 rhythm
N13 = N11 + 2 written-token surprise
N22 = N13 + 9: level, excess surprise, 3 change (one is a Mind-the-Gap-style drop), 4 shape
N40 = N22 + 18 history channels: entropy rhythm and drift
N53 = N40 + 13 copies, mostly of level
Each + 3 digit channels: N14, N16, N25, N43, N56.

We compare five label-free ways to fuse the same channels
All five see the same z-scored step channels of one bank and fit on one cell (one benchmark subset × scoring model) with no labels. They differ only in how they weigh the channels.
Name in this deck
What it does
Origin
Plain average
Mean of all channels as they are
Simplest reference
Oriented average
Flip each channel whose correlation with the mean of the 5 level channels is negative, then average
Fair control: same as plain, with label-free signs
IU-PCR
Estimate each channel's covariance with the hidden error from the channel covariance, then weight by 2 principal components
Dror et al. 2017, Tenzer et al. 2022; the project’s earlier main method
Continuous L-SML
Find groups of dependent channels, fuse inside each group by its leading eigenvector, then fuse the groups the same way
Jaffe et al. 2016; the project's earlier method
Our pipeline (4 variants)
Turn each channel into binary votes (its top 20% of steps vote "error"), drop wrong-way channels (Dawid–Skene), group, then weight groups (MoM)
New this round; variants differ in the within-group rule (MEAN, HEM, TCI) and vote unit (_cc: per channel, quota per cell; _ga: per group, quota per answer)
10 · Definitions used in every later result · method detail is in the second part of the deck · Deep dive: B12 pipeline, B4 fusion vs plain average
Our pipeline adds votes, a filter, groups and group weights to the plain average
1 · Read
Teacher-forced token probabilities of the given answer
2 · Channels
11 to 56 step features (one nested bank)
3 · Rescale
z-score each channel inside its own answer
4 · Vote
Each channel marks its top 20% steps as "error"
5 · Filter
Drop channels estimated worse than chance
6 · Group
Cluster channels that move together; merge near-duplicate groups
7 · Inside groups
Plain mean, learned weights (HEM) or a triplet (TCI)
8 · Between groups
Weight each group by its estimated accuracy (MoM)
9 · Score
Weighted sum of the group scores
10 · Decide
Which steps to flag, and whether the answer is clean
Four methods we compare differ in steps 4 and 7: votes per channel or per group, and a plain mean, HEM or TCI inside groups. All use MoM between groups (step 8).
Controls: the plain average of all channels stops after step 3. The oriented average adds a label-free sign. The filtered average stops after step 5.

Surprise at the written token works only when compared with an expectation
Written-token surprise = −log p of the token that is actually in the answer, under the scoring model. Read raw, it is weak. Compared with what the model expected, it becomes our strongest signal.
Channel
What it compares

Surprise z-test
The model's own forecast: (surprise − entropy) ÷ √varentropy, summed over the step

The recent past: smoothed surprise (EMA over 16 tokens), mean of the 3 sharpest rises in the step

How spread the model's forecast is; no written token

Why it works: entropy says how unsure the model is; the z-test asks whether the written token is more surprising than that uncertainty predicts. A sudden rise marks the place where the text stops matching what the model expects.
Checks: the surprise rise drops to 0.566 when tokens are shuffled, and keeps 0.771 after step length is removed. Step index alone is 0.662.

Varentropy was used to steer decoding; we found no prior test of it for finding the wrong step
Varentropy = how much the surprise of the next token varies under the model's own distribution: VE = Σ p·(−log p − H)². Our z-score uses it: z = (surprise of the written token − H) / √VE.
Prior work
Use
Tested against step-error labels?
Kontoyiannis & Verdú 2014
Defines varentropy (compression theory)
No; not about LLMs
entropix 2024 (code); Li et al. 2025, EACL 2026
Steer sampling and branching; spikes often match mistakes (39 of 50, manual count)
No benchmark
Fast-DetectGPT 2024; Min-K%++ 2025
Same z-score, without the name, for machine-text and pretraining-data detection
No; answer or document level
Katanemo blog 2025; LogitScope 2026
Flag possible hallucinations in tool calls or tokens
No labelled evaluation
What we can claim: first label-based evaluation of varentropy, and of the varentropy-scaled surprise, for locating the first wrong step on process benchmarks.
Our numbers: alone, varentropy channels reach 0.73 to 0.75 PRMBench AUC; the best (0.753) is clearly above entropy (0.730). They overlap strongly with the uncertainty level (correlation 0.91 to 0.94).

16 · Development data · "1 flag" = one flagged step per error-containing answer; it removes the clean-answer decision, where the PRM is strong · PANEL_B_PRMBENCH.csv, PANEL_B_CONTRASTS.csv · Deep dive: B7 supervised regression
PRMBench plants eight error types in three groups
Group
Error type: what is wrong
Real example: question → wrong step
Simplicity
Redundancy: a step adds nothing
√(x+7) = 9 → step 4 restates "x + 7 = 81" to re-confirm it
Circular logic: assumes the answer
98 × 102 → step 2: "Assume 98 × 102 = 9996 for verification"
Soundness
Counterfactual: breaks fact or arithmetic
88 ÷ 4 ÷ 2 → step 4: "Instead, let's multiply by 2"
Step contradiction: clashes with a past step
8xy²/6x²y → step 2 gives 72/36, step 3 says "1"
Domain inconsistency: wrong method
Factor 36 − 9x² → step 3 uses "the difference of cubes"
Confidence: wrong, stated as certain
C(15,3) → step 2: "654 with absolute certainty" (true: 455)
Sensitivity
Missing condition: drops a needed rule
LCM of 12, 18, 30 → step 5 takes 5², but 30 has only 5¹
Deception: a subtle, plausible error
Divisors of 18 → step 6: "1+2+3+6+9+18 = 38" (true: 39)

Label-free fusion ranks redundancy and circular-logic errors above the supervised PRM (80 of 80 and 72 of 80 configurations)
Ours ahead: redundancy, +0.13 to +0.22 AUC in all 80 configurations; circular logic in 72 of 80. 745 to 758 answers per type.
PRM ahead: confidence, counterfactual and deception in all 80. On confidence and deception, step index alone is above every label-free score: these errors sit late, and we do not use position.

No published method has its strength in redundancy and circular logic
The published profile
In about 40 PRMBench rows (paper, leaderboard, 5 later papers), every method above chance scores at least 4 points lower on redundancy and circular logic than on its soundness types. Human annotators are lower there too (by 3.4).
Qwen2.5-Math-PRM: about 20 points lower. It flags only 3.5% (7B) to 5.4% (72B) of redundant steps.
Best on these types
Redundancy: LLM judges asked for a redundancy score (Gemini-2.0-thinking 68.5); the best trained PRM is ReasonEval-7B, 61.0.
Circular logic: PRMs trained with error-type labels (PRISM-trained Qwen-PRM-7B 66.0, PathFinder 65.8). None leads on both.
Why, and our claim
PRM training data labels redundant steps "Neutral", so correctness PRMs pass them (PRMBench Appendix F).
Our claim: under the same protocol, label-free fusion ranks these errors above Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-7B. Not: "best on the leaderboard".

Where we lose: deciding that an answer is clean
The trade-off: a rule that flags enough steps to find errors also flags correct answers. Our top-20% rule leaves only 6% of correct answers clean; the count rule leaves 57%, but finds fewer errors.
Why it matters: PRMScore, ProcessBench F1 and Balanced F1 all reward leaving correct steps and answers alone. Here the supervised PRM is far ahead (0.89 left clean, F1 0.73).

On natural errors the signal still ranks the error step, but finds the exact step less often
Different kinds: 70% of the models' own first errors are misreadings, arithmetic slips and wrong methods. PRMBench never plants these.
Ranking holds, exact step drops: AUC 0.74 to 0.79 on those kinds, and similar to or above PRMBench where kinds overlap. But the top step is the first error in only 26% of answers (same score on ProcessBench GSM8K and MATH: 44%).

The two external sets: natural olympiad errors and LLM-inserted errors
Hard2Verify · natural errors
200 proofs by GPT-5, Claude Sonnet 4 and Gemini 2.5 Pro on recent olympiad problems (79 problems). Human math experts label every step. 42 proofs have no error. Metric: Balanced F1.
Example (described, not quoted): IMO 2024 Shortlist N6, proof by GPT-5, 5 steps. Step 1 claims that every n ≥ 2 works. The argument checks only one factor of the product and misses a second factor that is always even. Experts mark step 1 and all later steps wrong.
Socratic-PRMBench · planted errors
2,995 solutions: a correct solution (from a fine-tuned Qwen2.5-72B) into which GPT-4o inserts one typed error (20 types). Labels come from the edit; 10% spot-checked by people. Metric: PRMScore.
"Marcus is half of Leo's age and five years younger than Deanna. Deanna is 26. How old is Leo?"
3 ✓
Marcus's age = 26 − 5 = 21
4 ✗
"There seem to be some issues earlier, let me reconsider." … Marcus's age = 26 − 6 = 20
5–7 ✗
Leo's age = 2 × 20 = 40 (true answer 42)
In both sets we only score the given text: Qwen3-8B (and QwQ-32B for Socratic) reads each answer once by teacher forcing. Neither model wrote the answers.

Channels and their signs drive the score; the fusion rule matters little
We can say
  • On the best bank (N16), all label-free fusion rules land within 0.01 AUC, as at the answer level in August; across banks, getting signs right matters most
  • Channel choice moves the score more: +0.025 from 2 written-token channels; 18 rhythm channels cost −0.023, but nothing once their signs are corrected
  • No single channel is good on both benchmarks; fusion is
  • Label-free fusion ranks redundancy (80 of 80 configurations) and circular logic (72 of 80) above the supervised PRM
  • On PRMBench the top step is an error more often than with the PRM; on ProcessBench the PRM is far ahead (top-step hit 0.57 vs about 0.40)
  • With labels, the same channels gain 0.03 to 0.07 AUC on PRMBench, almost nothing on ProcessBench
We cannot say
  • That our new pipeline beats IU-PCR, continuous L-SML or the oriented average
  • Better than supervised PRMs overall, or "tied" on AUC
  • That the exact error step is found as often on natural errors (26%); ranking stays well above chance (AUC 0.785, error step vs all other steps)
  • First use of varentropy for hallucination detection; only for step-error localization
  • That the external results are a new test (labels opened before)

Next: lock the simplest recipe, test complementarity with the PRM, then confirm once
1 · Lock the simplest recipe
Default: oriented average, IU-PCR or continuous L-SML on a fixed bank, chosen by a rule written before any new data. The pipeline only if it shows a gain on the locked bank.
2 · Label-free + supervised
A fixed 50/50 average of our score and the cached PRM score, on PRMBench and ProcessBench. Tests whether the error-type profiles add up.
3 · Check natural errors; fix the clean-answer rule
I label about 40 of the own-answer error kinds by hand to validate the Claude labels. Separately, design a rule that leaves clean answers clean: with the top-20% rule, 94% of clean ProcessBench answers get a flag.
4 · Confirm on MedPRMBench
The only untouched set; needs new teacher-forced scoring (approval). Include step index, step length, oriented average, IU-PCR and L-SML from the start.
